facts.item: recent urgent care visit for an eye problem
facts.text: Two days ago I went to an urgent care center, and they thought I had conjunctivitis.
I used my EpiPen, but it didn't help.
I've been told I probably have pulmonary fibrosis (scarring of the lungs); that's why I take prednisone.

gold.reasoning: 1. Conjunctivitis was initially considered — “was prescribed polymyxin for presumed conjunctivitis.” 2. Anaphylaxis was considered given the oropharyngeal edema and patient’s self‐report — “she believed she was having an allergic reaction; after using her EpiPen® without resolution, she came to the ED to be treated.” 3. Bacterial or viral sinusitis or orbital cellulitis would explain early periorbital swelling — “the initial symptoms of rhinocerebral mucormycosis are usually mistaken for bacterial or viral sinusitis or orbital cellulitis.” 4. Upper respiratory and maxillary odontogenic infections were in the early differential — “infections such as sinusitis, and facial or orbital cellulitis, as well as upper respiratory and maxillary odontogenic infections, would be included in the differential.” 5. Intracranial infections, mass lesions, and cavernous sinus thrombosis were considered with cranial neuropathies — “If neurologic findings are present, then one must consider intracranial infections, mass lesions and cavernous sinus thrombosis.” 6. Rhinocerebral mucormycosis emerged as most consistent with the rapid progression in an immunosuppressed, acidotic patient — “The diagnosis of invasive fungal rhino-orbito cerebral mucormycosis became only suspected with development of proptosis, chemosis, vision loss and bilateral ophthalmoplegia.”

x009: The source gives only the interpretation ('a retinal pattern consistent with right central retinal artery occlusion'), with no description to fall back on, so it is kept.
x012: Diabetic ketoacidosis is reported without glucose, pH, bicarbonate or ketone values; the source's attribution to chronic steroid use is dropped as interpretation.
x013: Acute kidney injury is reported without creatinine values.

source_issues: s010: diabetic ketoacidosis is 'attributed to chronic steroid use' with no prior diabetes reported and no laboratory values.
s009: 'relative afferent pupillary defects' (plural) does not say which eye or both.
s001: the polymyxin route is not given.
notes: Index visit: the emergency department presentation with a swollen-feeling head and throat (s002-s006), two days after an urgent care visit for presumed conjunctivitis (s001), which is history.
s003: her own EpiPen use before arrival is a fact (f006); 'was treated for possible anaphylaxis without benefit' is treatment during the visit and is not used.
s006: the transfer for ophthalmologic assessment is process; the vision loss she reported is fact f003.

s007 and s008: the periorbital swelling, chemosis and the spread of ophthalmoplegia to bilateral cranial nerve III, IV and VI palsies over the next hours are kept as examination findings with time (x010, x011), not as patient facts.
s010: 'attributed to chronic steroid use' is clinician interpretation and is dropped from x012.
